direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very strong, following the classic Pixar Toy Story template, especially considering they know the world they are building with this being the fifth installment in the franchise; The direction on a microscale is also very strong as they know what they are doing, maintaining strong chemistry with the returning characters while integrating the new voice actors very well; The storytelling is very strong and keeps you fully engaged as the Pixar story team shows why they are the best in the business, keeping it somewhat fresh by telling the story through Jessie's perspective; The tension is good as it helps keep you emotionally engaged with the characters and what they are going through, but it definitely does not feel as strong as the rest of the franchise because it doesn't feel like there are any stakes anymore

performance.comments: Continues where he left off as Woody as he can performance this character in his sleep at this point; while he is more of a side character this time around, which makes me very sad, his voice acting acting is still top tier and adapts well to the new role; still has great chemistry with the rest of the cast, especially Tim Allen and Joan Cusack

Gives a strong performance as always, especially in the funny Buzz Lightyear army side plot, as he can basically do this character in his sleep; has strong chemistry with the rest of the cast, especially Tom Hanks and Joan Cusack

Really adapts to Jessie becoming the main character of the story as she really is the emotional core of the story as it it is told from her perspective, as it shows her doubt as a leader and her abandonment from her previous owners; has strong chemistry with the rest of the cast, especially Tom Hanks and Tim Allen
Feels like a great fit as he really is a dynamically funny character and his charisma really transfer well to the character, especially in a comedic way
Plays a very standard Pixar character, but does a good job with it and has good chemistry with the cast

cast.comments: The voice acting is strong as always, though it was kinda sad how the originally cast almost felt like cameos in this movie (but when you keep adding new members the gang, this was bound to happen); the cast has incredibly strong chemistry, and they did a great job of integrating the new voice actors alongside the returning cast.

story.comments: The concept is very relevant and fresh, focusing on the toys navigating a new world of technology as Bonnie becomes an iPad kid, which feels like a much better story than Toy Story 4; While this movie is still not needed after the franchise ended with Toy Story 3, they were able to find a way to continue the franchise and leave the door open for possible sequels instead of making it "the last Toy Story" like the previous two movies; The plot structure is pretty sound as it follows the Pixar Story template, but even though I enjoyed the Buzz Lightyear army side plot and thought it converged well with the main story in the end, it kind of just felt thrown in; The character writing is strong as they successfully make Jessie the emotional center and the main character, though Bonnie's character writing just makes her the absolute worst kid compared to Andy

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is very well-written, tight, and profound, showing why the Pixar creative team is the best in the business; The humor is good and quite funny, especially with the Buzz Lightyear side plot; The symbolism is very strong, dealing heavily with themes of feeling left out as a kid, feeling forgotten and no longer useful as a toy, and feeling abandoned; The foreshadowing is standard for what you expect from a Pixar family movie, so you can kind of expect what will happen because they are never going to go as dark as they did for Toy Story 3

score.comments: The score is very strong and continues the work Newman did on the past four movies; Since the movie is told from Jessie's perspective, it interpolates her main theme from Toy Story 2 a lot throughout the movie, and does so very well

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack is minimal but features a Taylor Swift song during the credits, which feels like a very obvious push by her and Pixar to get her an Oscar

editing.comments: This is very standard for a Pixar movie, as they know what they are doing and are not going to slip up on their bell cow

sound.comments: Well-executed and very standard for a Pixar movie, as they know what they are doing and are not going to slip up on their bell cow; It uses a lot of the same sound effects as the other Toy Story movies to help continue building this shared world

animation.comments: The animation is top-tier Pixar, featuring incredible detail, especially in the animal animation; I really liked the mixture of traditional Pixar 3D CGI with hand-drawn elements in the playtime moments, resembling the style of Puss in Boots: The Last Wish, which shows Pixar trying to innovate and remaining willing to adapt to the industry's shift toward hand-drawn styles

review.pacing: The pacing is strong and does not move too fast or too slow; I really did not feel like anything could have been cut, and I actually would have loved even more time with these characters because I just love them so much
review.climax: The climax is well-executed, though it is your typical high-speed action chase climax that almost all of the Toy Story movies have at this point, so it ends up being exactly what you expect from a Toy Story climax
review.tone: Tonally, it is what you would expect from a Pixar and Toy Story movie, continuing to build and tell more stories in this iconic world while helping to balance family humor with deep emotional resonance to leave a profound effect on you as you leave the theater and reminisce about your childhood toys stored in your mom's basement
review.overall: Overall, while I still feel like the franchise should have ended after 'Toy Story 3', 'Toy Story 5' is a well-executed Pixar movie that continues the legacy of the franchise by continuing to break ground with their animation, storytelling, and voice acting while also staying relevant and fresh as they shift the story from Woody and Buzz to Jessie's perspective and address more pertinent topics like iPad kids and abandonment, making this movie feel more profound than 'Toy Story 4'
